body:
OWNER RULING — APPROVED (2026-08-28)

Proceed with the tool-result governance design under these boundaries:

- Governance is optional through an explicit `disabled | shadow | enforce` mode. Disabled mode has no governance dependency.
- Policy selection is configuration-driven through named, versioned profiles. Mode controls disposition; profile controls classifiers, thresholds, corpus, redaction, and evaluation order.
- The first slice admits measured built-in profiles behind that stable seam. Arbitrary operator-authored policy definitions and per-tool bypass/exemption rules are deferred until corpus measurement justifies and bounds them.
- Unknown or unavailable non-disabled profiles fail explicitly at boot; there is no silent fallback.
- Governance applies consistently to every nonterminal external-content result before it enters model context, independent of tool name or effect declaration.
- Immutable raw completed outcomes and trajectory evidence remain intact; governance alters only the bounded model-visible copy.
- Shadow mode records the same decision without changing the model-visible content. Enforce mode applies the selected profile disposition.
- Do not introduce a new payload, stream, quarantine store, or general policy DSL merely for this slice.
- Terminal tool output that does not become a role=`tool` model input remains outside this issue.

The implementation must still pass the project architecture/reviewer gates, including restart, duplicate-delivery, correlation-key, and terminalization safety. This ruling settles product semantics; it does not waive those correctness requirements.

BLOCKER UPDATE — framework restart safety

The owner-approved ToolResult governance semantics remain binding: optional disabled/shadow/enforce mode, named/versioned built-in profiles, immutable raw evidence, and governance of the bounded model-visible copy.

Architecture review of approval-result correlation exposed a pre-existing critical framework defect now owned by #1146: agentic-loop persists `LoopEntity` but does not hydrate/reconcile its process-only context and correlation state after replacement, while several durable-input handlers ACK missing-state paths. The broader legibility/conformance contract is tracked by #1145 under epic #1147.

#1140 must not solve that systemic defect by inventing a private approval transaction manager, generic checkpoint bucket, or CQRS/event-replay path. Its independently valid classifier/profile/framing work survives, but enforcement, approval-pause recovery, and any restart-safety claim are blocked on #1146.

Blocked by: #1146.
